items.title: Pete Jolly interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999
items.q: So it was with Ava, and then Jackie Mills and Tommy Wolfe were running the company

ctx.x: So I said, “I really heard one little thing in your arrangement, and I transferred it and it became a tune.” So we recorded it. I played it for Bones Howe. And Bones Howe said, “Well I think I’ve got a company that will record you. It sounds like we’ve got something.” So it was with Ava, and then Jackie Mills and Tommy Wolfe were running the company, Fred Astaire owned it. It was originally Choreo — from Choreographer. That was the name of the company, but they had a lawsuit and somebody in Texas had that name,…
Yeah. I think it was originally released in ’62 and—
